questions.question_text: In $\log_{2}128$, which number is the argument?

options.why: named the base instead of the argument; the base is the small number written under the log
gave the value of the log ($2^{7}=128$) rather than the argument the log acts on

questions.solution_text:
The argument is the number the logarithm acts on, written after the base.
In $\log_{2}128$ the base is $2$ and the argument is $128$.

options.why: swapped the base and the argument when reading the log
read the logarithm as repeated multiplication instead of an index

questions.solution_text: $\log_{2}256$ means the power of $2$ that gives $256$, because $2$ is the base and $256$ is the argument.

options.why: gave the base $3$ instead of finding the power it is raised to
divided $81$ by $3$ rather than finding the power of $3$ that makes $81$

questions.solution_text:
$\log_{3}81$ is the power of $3$ that gives $81$.
$3^{4}=81$
$\log_{3}81=4$

options.text: No power of $2$ gives a negative number, so the argument cannot be $-32$.
The base $2$ is too small to reach $-32$.
options.why: blames the size of the base rather than the sign of the argument

options.text: $-32$ is not a power of $2$, but a decimal value still exists.
options.why: assumes any argument is allowed and only the neatness of the value is affected

questions.solution_text:
$\log_{2}(-32)$ asks for the power of $2$ that gives $-32$.
Every power of $2$ is positive, so no power gives $-32$. The argument of a logarithm must be positive, so the expression has no value.

questions.question_text: Which logarithm statement is equivalent to $2^{7}=128$?

options.why: used the index $7$ as the base instead of the base $2$
swapped the base and the argument
put the number $128$ and the index $7$ in each other's places
multiplied the base and the value ($3\times4$) instead of raising to a power
added the base and the value ($3+4$) instead of raising to a power
gave the base instead of the index that $a$ is raised to

questions.solution_text:
$\log_{a}a^{5}$ asks for the power of $a$ that gives $a^{5}$.
$a^{5}=a^{5}$
$\log_{a}a^{5}=5$
